headline: Engines convert energy from one form to another—usually heat to motion
universal_truth: Transformation is the key to usefulness; raw resources must be converted to serve purposes
fun_facts: Car engines are only about 25% efficient—75% of the fuel's energy becomes waste heat
The steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution, transforming society in decades
Your body is an engine too—converting food's chemical energy into motion and heat
discussion_questions: What different types of engines can you name?
Why is efficiency such a big concern with engines?
What 'engines' convert energy in your daily life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: An engine isn't magic—it's a converter. It takes energy locked in fuel and transforms it into motion. Whether burning gasoline or boiling water, engines do one job: convert one form of energy into another.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If engines convert energy from one form to another, why can't they convert all of it? Why is there always waste? Why can't we make a perfectly efficient engine?

options.text: Physics requires some energy to be lost as waste heat—entropy always increases
options.response: Yes. The second law of thermodynamics guarantees some energy is lost to disorder. Perfect efficiency is physically impossible.

options.text: We haven't invented the right materials or designs yet
options.response: Better materials help, but physics sets absolute limits. No engineering can overcome thermodynamics...

q1.title: Heat to Motion
q1.script: Most engines work by heating something—gas, steam, air—which expands and pushes. The expansion creates motion. Car engines burn fuel, steam engines boil water, jet engines compress and burn air. Heat becomes push.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Heat to Motion"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Revolutionary Power
q2.script: The steam engine, refined in the 1700s, powered the Industrial Revolution. Factories no longer needed rivers for water power. Trains connected cities. Ships crossed oceans reliably. One invention reshaped the entire world.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Efficiency Limits
q3.script: Car engines waste about 75% of fuel energy as heat. The best power plants reach maybe 60% efficiency. Physics sets hard limits—not all heat can become work. This is why efficiency improvements are so valuable.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Transformation is the key to usefulness. Engines teach that raw energy must be converted to serve purposes—and conversion always has costs. Nothing is free; everything is transformation.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 116. Tomorrow, we'll discover how computers think. Until then, notice the engines around you—the converters that power modern life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Energy Conversion - Notice Transformations
growTrack.activity: Identify three 'engines' you used today—devices that convert energy from one form to another. What goes in? What comes out? What's lost? Your car, your heater, even your body. Everything useful involves conversion.
